sentences.text:
In this petition, the petitioner - accused No.4 seeks quashing of the impugned proceedings in Crime
No.80/2023 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Sr. Dn.) and Cjm Court, Chikkaballapur
District, Chikkaballapur for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 408, 409, 420, 465, 466,
468, 471, 477 read with Section 34 of Ipc.
Heard the learned counsels for the parties and perused the material on record.

3. A perusal of the material on record will indicate that on 18.05.2023, the petitioner lodged a
complaint to the second respondent - the Assistant Commissioner, Chikkaballpur Sub- Division in
relation to fabrication of certain documents.

4.  It is grievance of the petitioner that instead of conducting any enquiry in relation to the complaint given by the petitioner on 18.05.2023, the second respondent filed the instant complaint on 19.06.2023 making allegations against accused Nos.1 to 3 viz., Mr. Rizwan Pasha, Mr. Maksood Pasha and Ms. Preethi.

It is pointed out that in the instant complaint which is registered as an FIR in Crime No.80/2023, except stating that the petitioner, who was working as a Second Division Sri. Abhilash T L vs State By on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23836970/

sentences.text: Assistant in the office of the Assistant Commissioner, Chikkaballapur, was only a case worker, no other allegations so as to make out a cognizable offence are forth coming in the said complaint qua the petitioner.

5. Under these circumstances, having regard to the material on record, in particular the complaint,
which merely states NC: 2025:KHC:657 that the petitioner was merely/only a co-worker and was not involved in the commission of any offence coupled with the fact that the petitioner himself had earlier filed a complaint bringing to the notice of the second respondent - the Assistant Commissioner the alleged fabrication of documents, I am of the considered opinion that the necessary ingredients for offences punishable under Sections 406, 408, 409, 420, 465, 466, 468,
471, 477 read with Section 34 of IPC are conspicuously absent in the complaint and consequently,
continuation of the proceedings as against the petitioner would tantamount to abuse of the process of law warranting interference by this Court in the present petition.

6. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is hereby allowed.

(ii) The impugned proceedings in Crime No.80/2023 on the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and CJM Court, Chikkaballapur District, Chikkaballapur for the offences punishable under Sections NC: 2025:KHC:657 406, 408, 409, 420, 465,
466, 468, 471, 477 read with Section 34 of IPC are hereby quashed.

Sd/-
